moduleTitle: Handling Advanced Mobile Automation Use Cases
learningObjectives: Explain how to run mobile tests in parallel using Tosca Commander and Distributed Execution for scalable automation.
Explain how mobile test execution scales beyond a single local machine.
Describe how executions are organised in Tosca Distributed Execution.
Explain what happens to an ExecutionList when it is uploaded to Tosca Cloud.
Recognise what changes for mobile specifically once execution is distributed or cloud-hosted.

elements.description: Mobile tests can run in parallel on multiple devices, and can use DEX or CI orchestration. Tosca Cloud artifact upload is a separate integration path; execution still depends on supported agents, connections and target infrastructure. Earlier local examples do not restrict the platform to one TestCase or device.

bulletPoints: Distinguish test orchestration, mobile target sessions and Cloud artifact copies.

elements.description: A TestEvent contains ExecutionLists and configurations. The Distribution Server assigns lists to Agents whose configuration matches; users can explicitly configure eligible Agents and lists. In Tosca 2026.1 LTS, DEX is no longer enabled by default and requires activation.

elements.title: The moving parts
items: TestEvent: groups ExecutionLists and their configurations for a distributed run.
Configurations: specify which matching Agent pool runs each list. Independent tests can be split with DEX/AOS setup and TCDistribution=True; repetitions are not supported for that split.
Agents execute the assigned work and need the application/files/connections required by those tests.
DEX Monitor provides execution status and cancellation controls.

elements.text: Agent matching does not replace mobile session configuration. For parallel mobile execution, verify licensing, target isolation and driver port requirements; dynamic target selection is not mandatory.

bulletPoints: TestEvents/configurations govern Agent assignment; DEX requires activation in 2026.1 LTS.
DEX/AOS test splitting and mobile session parallelism have distinct requirements.

elements.description: Upload creates a copy in the selected Tosca Cloud workspace, without bidirectional synchronization. A supported uploaded ExecutionList is represented as a playlist, available under Build > Playlists and Run > Playlists. Upload does not certify mobile execution readiness; infrastructure and permissions must still be configured.

elements.title: Playlist configuration and CI
items: Playlists can run on supported personal, team or cloud agents; Cloud orchestration does not imply every test runs on a vendor-hosted machine.
Configure sequence and Agent characteristics for the required environment.
The documented Jenkins workflow authenticates, starts a playlist run, polls status and retrieves JUnit results.

elements.text: Only changed selected objects can reduce re-upload work, but uploads overwrite existing Cloud objects and do not synchronize Cloud changes back. Check supported artifacts, excluded resources and version restrictions: TestEvents and configuration objects are excluded even though stored configuration TCP values can be included.

bulletPoints: An uploaded ExecutionList becomes a separate Cloud playlist copy.
Validate upload restrictions, Agent characteristics and run readiness.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What this means for mobile specifically

elements.term: Distribution raises the stakes on device configuration
elements.description: Plan separate usable targets and supported session/port configuration for concurrent runs. Fixed device assignment can be valid when targets are isolated; dynamic selection is an option, not a DEX/Cloud prerequisite. Application state and compatibility still need validation.

elements.text: Preserve orchestration, Agent, driver and Tosca evidence with timestamps and available session identifiers. A console is not necessarily gone, and one log source or ID is not guaranteed to reconstruct the whole run.

bulletPoints: Use supported isolated targets, parallel licenses and driver/session configuration.
Correlate available evidence; dynamic selection and a particular log source are not universal requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking DEX means manually assigning TestCases to agents
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Picturing Distributed Execution as a dispatcher where each TestCase is hand-allocated to a specific machine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use TestEvents/configurations to specify eligible Agent pools and ExecutionLists. This is explicit configuration, not a claim that users cannot select specific Agents.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming uploading to Tosca Cloud consumes or restricts the ExecutionList
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting an uploaded ExecutionList to be deleted after execution, to stay local-only, or to lock out other executions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Upload creates a separate supported Cloud copy/playlist; changes do not synchronize back and re-upload can overwrite Cloud objects. Configure actual execution infrastructure before running.

examPitfalls.title: Carrying single-device habits into distributed execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Moving TestCases that assume one pinned device, or that were only ever validated while someone watched LiveView, into a distributed or cloud-triggered setup.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate target isolation, effective configuration, licenses and diagnostics. Fixed targets can be valid; dynamic selection is not mandatory.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which objects organize ExecutionLists and matching Agent configuration in a Tosca DEX TestEvent workflow?

options.text: Only assigning individual TestCases by hand without TestEvents
Through direct execution in Tosca Commander
Using TestEvents and execution list configurations

practiceQuiz.hint: The question asks about the documented TestEvent workflow, not all possible trigger locations.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TestEvent groups ExecutionLists and configurations; the Distribution Server matches them to Agents. Commander can trigger the TestEvent, but a local direct run alone does not define this orchestration.

optionExplanations.A: Cloud artifact integration is separate from the named DEX workflow.
optionExplanations.B: Individual manual assignment alone does not define a TestEvent workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Commander can trigger DEX, but direct local execution alone does not organize matching Agent configurations.
optionExplanations.D: TestEvents contain ExecutionLists and configurations used for Agent matching.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After a successful supported ExecutionList upload to Tosca Cloud, what represents its organized tests in Cloud?

options.text: It gets converted into a Tosca Cloud playlist
It runs only on local machines

practiceQuiz.hint: The upload creates a Cloud copy; it does not synchronize both versions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The uploaded list’s tests are organized into a Cloud playlist. The original is not consumed; Cloud changes do not synchronize back. Running the copy still needs suitable infrastructure and permissions.

optionExplanations.A: The successful supported upload organizes the copied tests as a Cloud playlist.
optionExplanations.B: Upload does not consume/delete the original list after execution.
optionExplanations.C: Uploaded tests can use supported personal/team/cloud agents, not only local machines.
optionExplanations.D: Creating a playlist does not universally disable other executions.

quickRecap.value: TestEvents contain lists and configurations; the server matches Agent pools. DEX requires activation in 2026.1 LTS.
A supported upload creates a separate Cloud playlist copy, without bidirectional synchronization.
Configure sequence and Agent characteristics; Jenkins can authenticate, trigger, poll and retrieve JUnit results.
Parallel targets need isolation, licensing and driver ports. Fixed targets remain valid; dynamic selection is optional.
Preserve orchestration and execution evidence, timestamps and available session IDs; completeness is not guaranteed.
